description: High build epoxy resin floor coating
notFor: Do not apply the product directly on substrates with moisture content higher than 4% and/or with capillary rising damp
Do not apply Mapefloor FC 200 ME on dusty substrates.
Do not apply Mapefloor FC 200 ME on substrates with oil or grease stains or stains in general.
Do not dilute Mapefloor FC 200 ME with solvent or water
The air's relative humidity should not be greater than 75%

mixing: Mixing Ratio: Component A: Component B = 22: 3.5
packaging: 25.5 kg kits (component A = 22 kg; component B = 3.5 kg) in containers.
storage: The product must be stored in its original packaging in a dry place at a temperature of between +5°C and +35°C. Maximum 24 months.
notes: 1) The sheet gives consumption per coat for two systems (roll coat/structured: 0.32 kg/m² per coat; non-slip: 0.35-0.40 kg/m² per coat) but states no film thickness and no coverage per kit. The consumptionTable repeats the same two row labels (1st coat, Finishing coat) for system 1 and system 2, in that order. 2) The sheet says the rates are theoretical, calculated using Quartz 0.5, and that a larger sand will raise the consumption of the next coat; no figure is given for larger sand. 3) The application text says 'Fully broadcast with Quartz 0.5' while the consumption section gives 0.5-1.0 kg/m² for that broadcast. 4) Primer SN is quoted here at 0.15-0.25 kg/m², which differs from the Primer SN sheet (0.3-0.70 kg/m² per coat) and from the Mapefloor I 300 SL ME sheet (0.3 kg/m²). Priming is described as 'not normally required'. 5) Pot life reference temperature is inconsistent: the table heading says application data are at +23°C and 50% R.H., the body text says the pot life in the table refers to +25°C. 6) The technicalData 'Colour' value is the component A column (component B is printed as 'clear, light yellow'). 7) The Taber test value 95 is printed with no unit. 8) In the reading-order text file the final-performance values are detached from their labels; values were taken from the layout file. 9) No EN classification or CE standard is stated; only ASTM/EN test methods are cited in the data table, so standards is empty.
